submissions.title: Louisiana PSC kills ruling that would force Meta to turn over key data center information
submissions.excerpt: The commissioners voted 3-1 on Wednesday, in favor of overruling the judge, allowing Meta to withhold the information.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION / transparency development for tracked project 'Meta Hyperion' (slug meta-hyperion-louisiana, currently UNDER_CONSTRUCTION, ~5GW/$50B estimated). On Aug 12, 2026 the Louisiana PSC voted 3-1 along party lines to overrule an administrative law judge's July 10 subpoena order that would have forced Meta to disclose the methodology behind its stated job-creation and power-demand projections for Hyperion -- figures Entergy used to justify new gas-turbine applications for the site. Advocacy groups (Alliance for Affordable Energy, Sierra Club, Union of Concerned Scientists) sought the subpoena; Meta cited trade-secret protection. submissions.title: ERCOT aims to complete Texas governor's data center audit by December
submissions.excerpt: The audit and verification of data centers ordered by Gov. Greg Abbott will involve about 250 to 300 projects
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION update -- statewide, not tied to a single project. Extends Gov. Abbott's Aug 3, 2026 order halting new data-center grid interconnections in ERCOT territory pending an audit. At the Aug 20, 2026 PUCT open meeting, ERCOT laid out scope (~250-300 projects, mostly data centers, drawn from the interconnection queue) and timeline: RFIs Aug-Sep, information gathering/cure period Oct-Nov, Batch Zero Eligibility Verification Report + Community Impact Review Report due Dec 10, PUCT discussion at its Dec 17 meeting. This is a de facto statewide moratorium on new large-load grid connections in ERCOT, affecting the entire TX interconnection queue -- including tracked TX projects (e.g. Stargate Milam County, Stargate Shackelford County, Aligned Project Caprock, Compass Meridian, Fluidstack Abernathy, CoreWeave Lancaster). submissions.title: 'Project of unprecedented scale': Lake County residents file lawsuit to block 472-acre data center campus in Grayslake
submissions.excerpt: an electrical demand of approximately 1.55 gigawatts of power supplied by ComEd, with associated diesel backup generation
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION + likely NEW PROJECT not currently tracked. T5 @ Chicago IV, approved by the Grayslake, IL Village Board between Sept 2024 and May 2025: up to 472 acres, 10M+ sq ft of buildings, ~1.55 GW electrical demand from ComEd plus diesel backup generation. Sits within the broader $750M, 641-acre 'Cornerstone' mixed-use development -- that $750M figure is for the whole mixed-use development, NOT data-center-specific capex; do not enter it as this project's capex. On July 31, 2026 a group (Preservation of Community Well-Being Collective) and nine Lake County residents sued in circuit court to block the project, alleging Open Meetings Act violations and that data centers are not explicitly permitted under village zoning. On Aug 20, 2026 Grayslake announced then cancelled a public special session on the project, citing social media threats -- a live, escalating local fight worth watching. 1.55 GW is a site electrical demand figure (interconnection scale), not a confirmed IT load. submissions.title: Data center fight moves to NJ courts, with developers blaming local bans on 'public hysteria'
submissions.excerpt: Monroe Township in Gloucester County is facing a $300 million lawsuit from Hexa Builders LLC
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: a developer-litigation wave against local AI data center bans in New Jersey, all filed/active in recent weeks as of Aug 20, 2026. Monroe Township (Gloucester County) sued for $300M by Hexa Builders LLC over a zoning-rule change that blocked a proposed data center. Montgomery Township sued by E.
